evidence_packet.evidence_text: Warning: This article contains distressing content A woman who believed she had not had sex for nine years had in fact been regularly drugged and raped by her own husband and a group of strangers "whose depravity knew no bounds", a jury has been told Her husband led a "double life", prosecutors said, regularly giving his wife a "stupefying cocktail" of drugs to make her "completely unaware" of the abuse He and four men have already pleaded guilty to a series of offences, but the trial of nine other defendants who deny all charges has begun at Manchester Minshull Street Crown Court Opening the case for the prosecution, Louise Oakley KC said the wife had been "happy" but "the life she knew ended when the police knocked on the front door" Before the case was opened, trial judge Maurice Greene warned jurors they would be expected to view evidence that could provoke feelings of "upset and anger"

title: Michael Mullins: Family remember 'irreplaceable' head teacher

evidence_packet.title: Michael Mullins: Family remember 'irreplaceable' head teacher
evidence_packet.lead: Michael Mullins' family recall a devoted dad while colleagues describe how he helped transform a school
evidence_packet.summary: Michael Mullins' family recall a devoted dad while colleagues describe how he helped transform a school
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Michael Mullins: Family remember 'irreplaceable' head teacher - BBC News Image source, Family handout Image caption, Michael Mullins was described by his wife as "irreplaceable to family, friends, and the school" By Haider Saleem North West Published 2 November 2026 "Michael was my safety net," said Sarah Mullins as she described the loss of her husband, a head teacher who was murdered while cycling home from work. Michael Mullins, 56, loved music, was learning to play the guitar and would collect his daughter and her friends from concerts to make sure they got home safely. Colleagues said he had transformed Stretford Grammar School in Trafford, Greater Manchester, after becoming head teacher in 2009, when it was in special measures, and that his death had left "a void at every level". The tributes were heard at Manchester Minshull Street Crown Court as Simon Richardson, 35, was jailed for life with a minimum term of 25 years for murdering Mr Mullins on 20 April. Warning: This article contains distressing content Richardson struck Mr Mullins with his car in Warburton, Greater Manchester, before driving for more than a mile with the injured cyclist trapped underneath. Sarah described the many roles her husband had played in family life. "Michael was a cook, chauffeur, finance expert, quick to laugh and generous with time and money," she told Manchester Minshull Street Crown Court. "My past, present, and future have been brutally and callously torn apart." Image source, Family handout Image caption, Michael Mullins with his children, Harry and Maisie, who remembered him as a devoted father who always made time for them Their son, Harry, described his father as his best friend. title: Little Bollington data centre site owners ordered to restore farmland

evidence_packet.title: Little Bollington data centre site owners ordered to restore farmland
evidence_packet.lead: Cheshire East Council says some of the site needs to be returned to its original state
evidence_packet.summary: Cheshire East Council says some of the site needs to be returned to its original state
evidence_packet.evidence_text: The owner of land earmarked for a proposed data centre is facing action over failing to restore the site to its original state Land off Millington Road near Little Bollington, near Lymm, Cheshire, was used as a compound for vehicles working on upgrades to nearby motorways, and now forms part of a site on which a tech firm wants to build a large data centre compound Cheshire East Council said the enforcement notice against the Tatton Estate was not linked to the data centre plan, but campaigners against the 60-acre facility hope the council action will make it more difficult for the proposals to get planning permission Tatton Estate said it was appealing against the enforcement notice Data centres are typically large warehouses that store servers that process and distribute information online The artificial intelligence boom has coincided with a significant increase in the number of proposals to build them but the plans near Little Bollington are facing some opposition from nearby residents

title: War memorial statue depicting Jesus vandalised at Warrington church

evidence_packet.lead: The vandalism of a war memorial statue depicting Jesus Christ is being investigated as a hate crime
evidence_packet.summary: The vandalism of a war memorial statue depicting Jesus Christ is being investigated as a hate crime
evidence_packet.evidence_text: A war memorial statue depicting Jesus Christ has been vandalised at a Catholic church, with police investigating the incident as a hate crime Cheshire Police said the statue was damaged and daubed with graffiti on Friday at St Alban's Church in Bewsey, Warrington In a video released on the church's Facebook page, Canon Christopher Cunningham said the head of the figure had been "knocked off" in an incident of "true persecution". He said "offensive language against the Catholic Church" had been left on the statue's plaque The offensive language has since been removed by a church volunteer St Alban's Church declined to comment when contacted by the BBC The damage was discovered at 09:23 GMT on Sunday by a member of the congregation, police said

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Tram services were running as normal on Greater Manchester's Metrolink network again on Monday after two weeks of major disruption Improvement works have taken place at Deansgate-Castlefield and Trafford Bar, as well as in Manchester city centre, meaning no services ran on three Metrolink lines over that time A spokesman for Transport for Greater Manchester (TfGM) confirmed the work was on schedule to have been completed However, passengers have been warned that some minor route changes through the city centre will remain in place until Wednesday, with travellers advised to check the TfGM website , external Vernon Everitt, Greater Manchester's transport commissioner, told BBC Radio Manchester 's Hot Seat programme the works would be "the last big closures for a while" "Unfortunately there's never a good time to do these closures and I do apologise, but everyone will reap the benefits of it."

evidence_packet.evidence_text: "Michael was my safety net," said Sarah Mullins as she described the loss of her husband, a head teacher who was murdered while cycling home from work Michael Mullins, 56, loved music, was learning to play the guitar and would collect his daughter and her friends from concerts to make sure they got home safely Colleagues said he had transformed Stretford Grammar School in Trafford, Greater Manchester, after becoming head teacher in 2009, when it was in special measures, and that his death had left "a void at every level" The tributes were heard at Manchester Minshull Street Crown Court as Simon Richardson, 35, was jailed for life with a minimum term of 25 years for murdering Mr Mullins on 20 April Warning: This article contains distressing content Richardson struck Mr Mullins with his car in Warburton, Greater Manchester, before driving for more than a mile with the injured cyclist trapped underneath

evidence_packet.evidence_text: The owner of land earmarked for a proposed data centre is facing action over failing to restore the site to its original state Land off Millington Road near Little Bollington, near Lymm, Cheshire, was used as a compound for vehicles working on upgrades to nearby motorways, and now forms part of a site on which a tech firm wants to build a large data centre compound Cheshire East Council said the enforcement notice against the Tatton Estate was not linked to the data centre plan, but campaigners against the 60-acre facility hope the council action will make it more difficult for the proposals to get planning permission Tatton Estate said it was appealing against the enforcement notice Data centres are typically large warehouses that store servers that process and distribute information online The artificial intelligence boom has coincided with a significant increase in the number of proposals to build them but the plans near Little Bollington are facing some opposition from nearby residents

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Every morning for three weeks, Sarah Rimmer would call the hospital where her husband was fighting for his life in the hope of being told the father-of-two had simply made it through the night Lewis was in an induced coma after being knocked down by a Range Rover in the car park of a Sainsbury's store in Bolton, Greater Manchester - just moments after he bought a lottery ticket The doting father was airlifted to the Royal Preston Hospital where his family were told he had just a 30% chance of pulling through Lewis spent weeks on life support and had more than 40 hours of surgery, including the amputation of his left foot "For three weeks, I couldn't hear his voice, tell him about the girls or ask him for advice," said Sarah, reflecting on how life had changed one year on "The girls couldn't understand why we couldn't Facetime daddy."

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Was Shabana Mahmood forced into a U-turn over her migrant reforms? The Home Secretary has watered down her plans to make foreign care workers wait 15 years for settlement. But was it down to her own sense of "fairness" or did she capitulate to other C On Monday afternoon, Shabana Mahmood addressed the Commons by discussing a deeply personal account of her own family’s migration to the UK 50 years ago from rural Kashmir “They came here knowing one thing above all else – that they would be treated fairly here,” she told Parliament. “They came from a place where power was often arbitrary and where the dice were always loaded. They came to this country because they knew we do things differently her It was an appeal to the values the Home Secretary believes underpins Britain’s immigration system – a sense of fairness Ms Mahmood reiterated those views when she announced her reforms on migration She said a five-year path to settlement will remain open for those earning over £50,000, and those earning 125,000 would get a fast-track route to settlement after just three years

Mr Burnham was then collected at Manchester along with his wife, Ma Former prime minister Gordon Brown was also on the Government plane. The Guido Fawkes website estimated the cost of the Stansted-Manchester flight as £20,000 But the Prime Minister's spokesperson defended the decision and said security, operational reasons and value for money for the taxpayer were all considerations when deciding on how the Prime Minster travels. The spokesperson said: “The Prime Minister’s travel arrangements are mad "The Prime Minister’s travel arrangements reflect where he was carrying out official government business at the end of last week. He spent the day in Scotland on Friday, returned to Manchester to work from Number 10 North on Friday evening.”

Mark Vernal sadly died in hospital after he was trapped in a blaze at his family home on Dumbarton Green in Wigan on August 14, 2024 An inquest into his death began at Bolton Coroners Court on Monday (November 2) Several members of Mark’s family attended the court, including representatives of Greater Manchester Police and Wigan Council. His killer, Simon Richardson, struck Mr Mullins at the junction of Dunham Road and Warburton Lane in Partington, on April 20 this year Mr Mullins was then dragged underneath Richardson's Volvo for 2.2km - or 1.3 miles - before dying at the roadside on Wet Gate Lane in Lymm. Minshull Street Crown Court heard that Richardson had previously made 'physical concerted efforts' to remove Mr Mullins from under his car b Richardson, 35, then drove away from the scene, later swapping his car for a silver van. The following day he was finally caught up with after leading police on a high speed pursuit through Failsworth Following a two week trial, jurors found him guilty of murder and dangerous driving. Today, November 2, he was jailed for life to serve a minimum term of 25 years

title: Was Shabana Mahmood forced into a U-turn over her migrant reforms?

evidence_packet.title: Was Shabana Mahmood forced into a U-turn over her migrant reforms?
evidence_packet.lead: Was Shabana Mahmood forced into a U-turn over her migrant reforms?
evidence_packet.summary: Was Shabana Mahmood forced into a U-turn over her migrant reforms? The Home Secretary has watered down her plans to make foreign care workers wait 15 years for settlement
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Was Shabana Mahmood forced into a U-turn over her migrant reforms? The Home Secretary has watered down her plans to make foreign care workers wait 15 years for settlement. But was it down to her own sense of "fairness" or did she capitulate to other C On Monday afternoon, Shabana Mahmood addressed the Commons by discussing a deeply personal account of her own family’s migration to the UK 50 years ago from rural Kashmir “They came here knowing one thing above all else – that they would be treated fairly here,” she told Parliament. “They came from a place where power was often arbitrary and where the dice were always loaded. They came to this country because they knew we do things differently her It was an appeal to the values the Home Secretary believes underpins Britain’s immigration system – a sense of fairness Ms Mahmood reiterated those views when she announced her reforms on migration She said a five-year path to settlement will remain open for those earning over £50,000, and those earning 125,000 would get a fast-track route to settlement after just three years

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Greater Manchester Police New arrest made in 'HMO' attacks probe after properties targeted across Greater Manchester A total of eight people have now been detained following spate of vandalism across Greater Manchester Add to preferred sources News Da Police have made another arrest as a probe into a spate of vandalism and criminal damage against HMOs across Greater Manchester continues. Greater Manchester Police launched an investigation into dozens of suspected incidents across Salford , Tameside , Bolton , Rochdale , Wigan The force said previously it had received 46 reports of criminal damage to properties that are either houses of multiple occupation, or properties being mistaken for HMOs, since October 5. In some of the incidents, homes had 'no HMO' sprayed onto their front doors Cars were also smashed and windows broken. This morning (Monday) a 29-year-old man was arrested on suspicion of conspiracy to commit criminal damage in connection with the attacks Chief Supt Marcus Noden previously said police believe that vulnerable people, including children, have been exploited and paid to damage buildings. He said: "Our relentless pursuit of those causing or facilitating this recent spate of damage is not letting up as we continue to e "One area of focus continues to be our belief that vulnerable people - including children - are being exploited and paid to damage buildings. If you know anything that could help us, we're continuing to urge you to come forward and speak to us

evidence_packet.summary: Rochdale Banned driver led police on high-speed chase through the streets of Rochdale Bilal Ishaq reached speeds more than three times the limit as he tried to outrun police motorcyclists in a black Mercedes Add to preferred sources News Damon Wilkins Police footage shows officer
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Rochdale Banned driver led police on high-speed chase through the streets of Rochdale Bilal Ishaq reached speeds more than three times the limit as he tried to outrun police motorcyclists in a black Mercedes Add to preferred sources News Damon Wilkins Police footage shows officers take up the pursuit on Foxholes Road after they suspected the 35-year-old of drug dealing. In the clip an officer can be heard saying 'It's a black Mercedes, believe he's drug dealing' Ishaq can then be seen racing through residential streets at speeds of over 60mph. At one point he goes through a mini-roundabout on the wrong side of the road, narrowly avoiding a car pulling out from a side street He also ran red lights and twice attempted to reverse into the police riders. As the pursuit comes to an end he pulls over and attempts to run away, as the abandoned Mercedes rolls down the street with the drivers door still open Ishaq, of Hey Street, Rochdale, who was already serving two court-imposed driving bans following a separate dangerous driving offence in December 2025, was arrested shortly afterwards He later admitted dangerous driving, driving whilst disqualified, failing to stop and driving without insurance and was jailed for 16 months and disqualified from driving for five years

"In many cases, they demand payment for work that is either unnecessary, significantly overpri There has been an increase in fraud reports over recent weeks. title: Was Shabana Mahmood forced into a U-turn over her migrant reforms?

evidence_packet.title: Was Shabana Mahmood forced into a U-turn over her migrant reforms?
evidence_packet.lead: Was Shabana Mahmood forced into a U-turn over her migrant reforms?
evidence_packet.summary: Was Shabana Mahmood forced into a U-turn over her migrant reforms? The Home Secretary has watered down her plans to make foreign care workers wait 15 years for settlement
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Was Shabana Mahmood forced into a U-turn over her migrant reforms? The Home Secretary has watered down her plans to make foreign care workers wait 15 years for settlement. But was it down to her own sense of "fairness" or did she capitulate to other C On Monday afternoon, Shabana Mahmood addressed the Commons by discussing a deeply personal account of her own family’s migration to the UK 50 years ago from rural Kashmir “They came here knowing one thing above all else – that they would be treated fairly here,” she told Parliament. “They came from a place where power was often arbitrary and where the dice were always loaded. They came to this country because they knew we do things differently her It was an appeal to the values the Home Secretary believes underpins Britain’s immigration system – a sense of fairness Ms Mahmood reiterated those views when she announced her reforms on migration She said a five-year path to settlement will remain open for those earning over £50,000, and those earning 125,000 would get a fast-track route to settlement after just three years

Greater Manchester Police launched an investigation into dozens of suspected incidents across Salford , Tameside , Bolton , Rochdale , Wigan The force said previously it had received 46 reports of criminal damage to properties that are either houses of multiple occupation, or properties being mistaken for HMOs, since October 5. In some of the incidents, homes had 'no HMO' sprayed onto their front doors Cars were also smashed and windows broken. This morning (Monday) a 29-year-old man was arrested on suspicion of conspiracy to commit criminal damage in connection with the attacks Chief Supt Marcus Noden previously said police believe that vulnerable people, including children, have been exploited and paid to damage buildings. He said: "Our relentless pursuit of those causing or facilitating this recent spate of damage is not letting up as we continue to e "One area of focus continues to be our belief that vulnerable people - including children - are being exploited and paid to damage buildings. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Rochdale Banned driver led police on high-speed chase through the streets of Rochdale Bilal Ishaq reached speeds more than three times the limit as he tried to outrun police motorcyclists in a black Mercedes Add to preferred sources News Damon Wilkins Police footage shows officers take up the pursuit on Foxholes Road after they suspected the 35-year-old of drug dealing. In the clip an officer can be heard saying 'It's a black Mercedes, believe he's drug dealing' Ishaq can then be seen racing through residential streets at speeds of over 60mph. At one point he goes through a mini-roundabout on the wrong side of the road, narrowly avoiding a car pulling out from a side street He also ran red lights and twice attempted to reverse into the police riders. As the pursuit comes to an end he pulls over and attempts to run away, as the abandoned Mercedes rolls down the street with the drivers door still open Ishaq, of Hey Street, Rochdale, who was already serving two court-imposed driving bans following a separate dangerous driving offence in December 2025, was arrested shortly afterwards He later admitted dangerous driving, driving whilst disqualified, failing to stop and driving without insurance and was jailed for 16 months and disqualified from driving for five years

evidence_packet.evidence_text: How a sweatshop empire is Manchester-washing its reputation “I can’t always be in LA,” reads one TikTok caption, “someone has to hold it down in Rochdale.” It’s written over a model strutting through a leatherwear shoot. She’s wearing Musera, which looks to be Manchester’s friendliest, chicest new clothing label — launched in 2024 from an From this Newton Street office, a band of young designers turn out a stream of trend pieces: low-rise trousers and asymmetric tops, distressed knitwear and leopard-print flares, western fringed jumpers and A-level prom gowns. Their Instagram bio lauds the brand as “Est. MCR.” Over a million people watched the staff dancing around their Northern Quarter office to Whigfield’s Saturday Night on TikTok. More still tuned in to a video showing them kitted out in Musera for Drake’s performance at Co-op Live last year. And who knows how many have sidestepped “Be a muse in your own era,” goes their slogan; presumably also the source of their similarly recondite name. Their Instagram captions are a list of internet cliches verging on parody. “My blood type is iced latte,” reads one post Looking at this well-curated online presence, you might well be convinced that Musera is, as they suggest, Manchester through and through

evidence_packet.lead: A driver who dragged a head teacher to his death for more than a mile under the wheels of his car has been jailed for life for murder Simon Richardson, 35, crashed into 56-year-old Michael Mullins in Warburton, Greater Manchester, on 20 April as the married father-of-two cycled h
evidence_packet.summary: A driver who dragged a head teacher to his death for more than a mile under the wheels of his car has been jailed for life for murder Simon Richardson, 35, crashed into 56-year-old Michael Mullins in Warburton, Greater Manchester, on 20 April as the married father-of-two cycled h
evidence_packet.evidence_text: A driver who dragged a head teacher to his death for more than a mile under the wheels of his car has been jailed for life for murder Simon Richardson, 35, crashed into 56-year-old Michael Mullins in Warburton, Greater Manchester, on 20 April as the married father-of-two cycled home from Stretford Grammar School in Trafford Jurors at Richardson's trial heard he then stopped to try to dislodge the injured but still-living cyclist before driving on with him still lodged underneath the vehicle The judge at Manchester Minshull Street Crown Court told Richardson that he would have to serve a minimum of 25 years in prison Richardson had previous convictions for 28 offences, with a "significant history" of driving-related crimes He was also on bail at the time of the murder for offences including affray and assault occasioning actual bodily harm

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Primary schools have been recognised for outstanding performance in the 2026 Summer Reading Challenge Read to the Beat. Royton Hall Primary School, St Martin’s Primary School and Greenfield Primary School were recognised as the schools with the highest participation out of 92 schools taking part across Oldham. Representatives from Oldham Libraries and partner Kajima, which supports opportunities to encourage children to read and celebrate their success, visited each school to award book tokens in recognition of pupils’ commitment to reading. Kajima have sponsored the Summer Reading Challenge for the sixth year running, encouraging Oldham children towards a lifelong love of books. The challenge highlights the importance of partnerships between schools, libraries and local organisations in supporting children’s literacy, building reading confidence and making reading an exciting and rewarding experience. evidence_packet.evidence_text: An exciting new visitor attraction has opened its doors in the heart of Oldham. The first phase of Northern Roots is now open, marking an exciting chapter at the home of what will be the UK’s largest urban farm. Delivered through a partnership between the Northern Roots charity and Oldham Council, the new 160-acre development gives people the chance to enjoy nature closer to home, improving local health and wellbeing, supporting education, creating local jobs, and playing an important role in Oldham's ongoing regeneration. The project is transforming 160-acres of underused land next to Alexandra Park into a landmark destination, and the opening day gave visitors their first opportunity to experience the Welcome Building, cafe, Forestry Skills Centre, Urban Farm, and an expanding network of trails, orchards, woodland and wetlands. Thousands of visitors from across Oldham and beyond flocked to the site to experience Oldham’s newest major visitor attraction. Families enjoyed an outdoor play area with a sandpit, climbing frames and water play, and free activities including face painting, outdoor games, live music, a bubble performer, unicyclist and roaming stilt walkers. They could explore Snipe Clough Farm, a new four-acre working urban farm, and make wildflower seed bombs with the friendly team of volunteers. One family, who travelled over from Stockport for the opening, said: "It's really nice to see sustainable projects like this. It's a great day out for the family." And Sami Al-Othman from Stretford said: "It's great. This is what's needed everywhere. We're always looking for new things to do with the kids so this is perfect." title: Oldham Council agrees interim Lead Member arrangements to strengthen governance and accountability

evidence_packet.title: Oldham Council agrees interim Lead Member arrangements to strengthen governance and accountability
evidence_packet.lead: Oldham Council has approved a new package of interim governance arrangements
evidence_packet.summary: Oldham Council has approved a new package of interim governance arrangements
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Oldham Council has approved a new package of interim governance arrangements. These measures are designed to strengthen democratic oversight, provide clear political leadership across key service areas and support transparent decision-making while the borough continues to work towards the appointment of a Council Leader and Cabinet. The arrangements were approved by Council on 16 September and include the creation of interim Lead Member and Deputy Lead Member roles aligned to the Council's four directorates. The arrangements form part of a wider governance framework developed following legal advice, engagement with the Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government, and discussions between political group leaders. Under the arrangements, Chief Executive Shelley Kipling will continue to exercise delegated executive powers, while Lead Members provide political oversight, advocacy and a visible link between residents, councillors and services. The roles carry no executive decision-making powers. evidence_packet.title: Work starts at illegal waste site following appointment of main contractor
evidence_packet.lead: Acumen Waste Service Limited have started preparatory works to remove the illegally deposited waste at Bolton House Road Following a robust tender process, Wigan Council announced that it had chosen Acumen as its preferred contractor last month, with contracts now officially sign
evidence_packet.summary: Acumen Waste Service Limited have started preparatory works to remove the illegally deposited waste at Bolton House Road Following a robust tender process, Wigan Council announced that it had chosen Acumen as its preferred contractor last month, with contracts now officially sign
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Acumen Waste Service Limited have started preparatory works to remove the illegally deposited waste at Bolton House Road Following a robust tender process, Wigan Council announced that it had chosen Acumen as its preferred contractor last month, with contracts now officially signed after a compulsory standstill period Acumen is bringing in equipment and clearing vegetation at the Bickershaw site to allow waste to start being removed in the coming weeks Councillor Nazia Rehman, Leader of Wigan Council, said: “The contract signing and mobilisation at Bolton House Road is a clear sign of progress and a significant moment for the community who have had to deal with the impact of the illegal waste site “Reaching this stage also demonstrates the commitment of the council and partners to deliver the necessary framework for waste clearance, but our work does not stop here “We will continue to work with residents to ensure their voice is heard in the future of the site and will continue to support the Environment Agency’s criminal investigation to make sure those responsible are held accountable for the damage and distress they have caused.”

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Experience the raw, unfiltered power of Balkan folklore in a new immersive show from the world’s most famous performance artist Balkan Erotic Epic is a bold new performance work created by the iconic artist Marina Abramović . Regarded as the world’s most influential performance artist, Abramović’s transformative work has reached millions of people – from opening the Pyramid Stage at Glastonbury Festival t A four-hour ritual where ancient myth meets performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic explores the eroticism, spirituality and traditions of Abramović’s homeland through 13 visceral scenes Brought to life by a cast of over 70 performers, dancers, musicians and singers, the experience unfolds across Aviva Studios. Audiences are free to choose their own path – with pop-up encounters punctuating the action, bringing bodies together in dance, song and ritual Watch Fertility Rite , a fevered ritual where bodies writhe against the ground in a desperate call for fertility. Witness Massaging the Breast where women gesticulate over graves to awaken the earth. In Scaring the Gods , women bare themselves to the sky to banish storms. Listen Unafraid to push the boundaries of eroticism and performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic asks its audience a timeless question: What are our bodies truly for?

From a childhood in exile to surviving secret detention in China, his remarkable life and career have led him to global prominence. Using sculpture, installation, film, photography In Button Up! , the artist turns his lens on two centuries of Chinese and British relations. The monumental installation features porcelain, cotton, glass, bronze and even buttons and toy bricks. Each material contains a stor Both global and personal, the title Button Up! is a playful poke at the artist’s ongoing battle with censorship. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Finish work and unwind with live music from Manchester’s best jazz musicians. Beat the Jams live series showcases the very best of the jazz scene, at short rush hour gigs from 6pm at Band on the Wall. What better way to avoid those endless queues, chaotic traffic and stressful homeward journeys? Clock off and skip the rush-hour traffic while you watch live jazz and make the most of our happy hour deals from 5–7pm: £4.50 pints / 2 for £15 cocktails / £15 bottles of wine + pizzas from £5! The new season kicks off on 24 September with tenor saxophonist Dean Masser and pianist Richard Wetherall, followed by: 7 October – Anna Chandler-King Quartet Leeds based saxophonist and composer Anna joins us again for Beat the Jams, this time with her own band. Anna’s thoughtful and inventive compositions are firm favourites of us at Beat the Jams and her quartet promises to be a unique rush hour busting treat! 16 November – Sam Lightwing Quartet Saxophonist and composer Sam Lightwing brings presents brand new music for his thrilling young quartet, showcasing Sam’s original compositions, which blend classic mainstream jazz grooves with modern flavours of post-pop and latin, all wrapped up in the language of contemporary sax giants such as Chris Potter, Seamus Blake and Joshua Redman. 15 December – Svarc/Devine/Walsh with Richard Iles The band combines deep pocket, fearless interplay and a shared love of exploration. Expect everything from soulful melodies and infectious rhythms to moments of exhilarating collective improvisation, delivered with the chemistry that only world-class musicians can create. Tickets from £13 per show, or £42 for a season ticket

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Mr Thomas’s Chop House has been part of Manchester since 1867. A £300,000 restoration, long-term lease and 23-year-old head chef are shaping what comes next Go to Manchester's Finest X profile Mr Thomas’s Chop House has been serving Manchester since 1867, but owner Roger Ward admits there was a point after Covid when he wasn’t sure how much longer he wanted to keep doing it Tom’s had gone eight years without a proper lease and much longer without any meaningful investment by the landlord. Retirement was being seriously considered. Instead, Roger decided to “go again properly” That decision has resulted in a new long-term commitment to the Chop Houses and around £300,000 being spent restoring Tom’s – touching everything from the dining rooms and furniture to the menu, wine list, kitchen and beer cellars Roger is particularly pleased with the toilets “Tom’s was famous for the shittest toilets in town,” he says. They are now, by his assessment, considerably less so. Downstairs has been redone, upstairs has new ones too, while a previously overlooked back room has been completely reworked

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Counter Manchester will open its doors on Monday 9th November at 12pm, marking the group’s first opening in Manchester city centre and bringing a theatrical approach to dining to the heart of the city Led by acclaimed chef Andrew Sheridan, Counter will be located in Manchester’s Island Building on John Dalton Street, with 60 covers. The opening marks Open Restaurant Group’s 9th restaurant to date and its second site in Greater Manchester, following the launch of Arcadian in Di At the heart of the restaurant will be a four-to-five-seat chef’s counter, placing guests directly at the pass for an up-close view of the kitchen in action. evidence_packet.evidence_text: The government's new Digital and Technologies Jobs Plan aims to create 200,000 entry-level jobs over the next decade, recognising the barriers facing employers and the importance of regional organisations in connecting people with opportunities. The government has published its D The plan acknowledges that the challenge is not simply a shortage of people with digital skills. Entry-level recruitment has become more difficult, with employers increasingly favouring experienced candidates and many graduates and other new entrants struggling to secure their fi Manchester Digital contributed to the development of the plan through its involvement in the government's Digital Skills Council, drawing on its work with employers and education providers across Greater Manchester Around 800,000 digital and technology roles are projected to need filling over the next decade. The plan sets out an ambition to create 200,000 entry-level jobs, including apprenticeships, during that period The plan also addresses how AI is changing workforce requirements and the importance of ensuring people entering the industry have both technical knowledge and practical workplace skills Manchester Digital's 2026 Sector Insights Report highlighted a reduction of around 20% in early-career opportunities, despite continued demand for experienced technology professionals

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Manchester will mark Remembrance Sunday with its annual city centre service this November Honouring the service and sacrifice of members of the Armed Forces community, the commemorative event is open to all and will take place on Sun 8 Nov at the Manchester Cenotaph in St Peter’s Square between 10.30am and 12pm At 10.30am veterans, serving military personnel and cadets, led by the Greater Manchester Police Band, will march from John Dalton Street to the Cenotaph At 10.45am, the civic procession will set off from Mount Street, accompanied by the Scots Guards Association Pipe Band, making its way to the Cenotaph ahead of the service At 10.58am, the service will begin. Written about the life and paintings of L. S. Lowry, it turned one of the region’s best-known artists into an unlikely pop culture ph Coming to Lowry this November, Matchstalks Remastered is a playful music-theatre performance inspired by the song, the artist and the city that connects them. Two performers, accompanied by live jazz musician Adam Fairhall and a record player, attempt to follow a constantly scrol As the record plays, movement, storytelling and slapstick collide. Kevin Egan and Michael Pinchbeck shift between performers, songwriters, Lowry himself and the familiar figures populating his paintings, using the structure of the original song to create a series of theatrical sc Along the way, the production follows Lowry’s footsteps around Manchester and plays with the way stories about artists are remembered and retold. How does a painting become a song? What happens when that song becomes theatre? And what gets lost, exaggerated or reinvented along th The performance also arrives in the year marking the 50th anniversary of Lowry’s death, offering an appropriately unconventional way to revisit an artist whose industrial landscapes remain closely tied to the identity of Greater Manchester

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Bolton Car Boot Sale is one of the North West's biggest weekly boot sales, held in the hardstanding car park of the Macron Stadium (formerly Reebok), Burnden Way, Horwich, Bolton BL6 6JW. It runs every Sunday from February right through to December, drawing over 300 sellers and thousands of bargain hunters each week. Sellers can arrive and set up from 6:00 AM, with buyers welcomed in from 7:00 AM. Entry costs just £1 per car for buyers. Pitches for sellers are £14 for a car, £20 for a van and £3 for a trailer, with regular and corner pitches available on request. Bring exact change to keep the queue moving, and call organiser Andrew on 07470784644 for more details. Expect hundreds of stalls across the concrete hardstanding pitches, so it goes ahead in most weather. On-site you'll find a 5-star catering service, doughnuts and coffee, ice cream and desserts, a meat auction, fresh fruit and veg, plants, and retro sweet stalls. The sale is dog-friendly, has male and female toilets, ample parking, and kids' rides and bouncy castles to keep little ones entertained. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Football Manchester United FC LIVE Updated 19 mins ago Man United news LIVE: Michael Carrick sack deadline set as Eddie Howe makes decision Pressure remains on Manchester United boss Michael Carrick ahead of tonight's Champions League clash vs AS Roma. ( Image: Phil Duncan/ It's another big week for Manchester United as they are back in Champions League action. Michael Carrick will be in charge of the team for tonight's home clash against AS Roma, despite the continued pressure on the United boss United will be looking to get back to winning ways. A 2-0 defeat against Chelsea on Saturday means that the team are winless in their last nine games in all competitions It's led to a lot of questions being asked over the future of Carrick, although reports suggest that the situation will be reviewed during this month's international break. Following the game vs Roma, United host Aston Villa at Old Trafford on Sunday (4.30pm kick-off) Former Newcastle United manager Eddie Howe has been named as a potential option for United, should they opt to make a change. Latest reports suggest that he would be open to taking the role Stay here for all of the latest throughout the day

evidence_packet.evidence_text: 8 ноября 2026 года в Indigo at The O2 состоится концерт GORAN BREGOVIC в Лондоне Имя Горана Бреговича давно стало символом целого музыкального мира. Его путь начался в многонациональном Сараеве, где восточные мотивы естественно переплетались с западными традициями, а каждая улица имела свой ритм. Сотрудничество с режиссером Emir Kusturica подарило мировому кинематографу саундтреки, ставшие неотъемлемой частью фильмов Time of the Gypsies, Arizona Dream и Underground. В этих мелодиях живут Балканы — с их своб Популярность Бреговича родилась не только благодаря знаменитым композициям “Kalashnikov”, “Ederlezi”, “In the Death Car” или “Bella Ciao”. Его главный талант — превращать народные мотивы в современное искусство, не теряя их подлинной силы. Город, который веками принимал выступления и разные культуры со всех континентов, на один вечер станет местом встречи британской сдержанности и безудержной балканской страсти.
